diagnosis.summary: The pod probefail-b886c94bd-kbp2p is in CrashLoopBackOff with 193 restarts. The root cause is a failing liveness probe: the container app is not listening on TCP port 8080, causing Kubernetes to repeatedly kill and restart it (exit code 137 = SIGKILL from liveness probe failure). The previous container log is empty, indicating the app either never starts a listener or exits before one is established. The node oncall-worker2 rebooted recently but recovered and is Ready; the liveness probe failures predate the reboot by days.

hypotheses.mechanism: The liveness probe performs a TCP connect to port 8080 on the container. The probe consistently fails with 'connection refused' (F4), causing Kubernetes to kill the container (exit code 137, F1) and log 'Container app failed liveness probe, will be restarted' (F12). This cycle has been ongoing since at least 2026-10-05, accumulating 193 restarts and over 1000 BackOff events (F3). The previous container emits no logs (F11), suggesting the app process either never binds to port 8080 or crashes before doing so. The container lifetime of only 58 seconds (F1) is consistent with a probe kill rather than an immediate crash.

Check current container stdout/stderr to see if the app is starting and whether it binds to port 8080.

remediate.action: Fix the application so it listens on the port the liveness probe targets (TCP 8080), or correct the liveness probe port/path in the Deployment spec to match the port the app actually binds to. If managed by Argo CD or Helm, make the change in the source repository and let it sync.

If the liveness probe thresholds are too aggressive (initialDelaySeconds too short), increase initialDelaySeconds and failureThreshold in the Deployment spec to give the app time to start before probing begins.
Delete the stuck pod to allow a fresh start once the spec is corrected, clearing the CrashLoopBackOff back-off timer.

If the app crashes before it ever opens port 8080, the liveness probe would see 'connection refused' and kill the container — producing the same observable symptoms as a misconfigured probe. Exit code 137 is consistent with a SIGKILL from the probe, but an app that crashes before the probe fires would also result in a restart. The short 58-second lifetime (F1) and empty logs (F11) are consistent with either scenario.
